intro: A target network can move more slowly than the model being optimized. Its update rate controls how much of a newly learned parameter vector is copied at each synchronization.
task: Compute a fresh target parameter array and compare a frozen target, a partial update, and a hard copy.
requirements: target and online are matching nonempty vectors or matrices, with every axis length in 1..256. rate is a scalar in [0,1].
Return (1-rate)*target+rate*online as a new NumPy array. Here rate weights the online parameters; some literature instead names the target retention coefficient.
Rate zero preserves the target values, rate one copies the online values. Never change either input in place, including endpoint cases.

Use real finite numeric inputs of magnitude at most 1e30, excluding boolean parameters. Vectors have 1..256 entries and each matrix axis has length 1..256 unless a stricter bound is stated. Leave caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Identify which coefficient is named
hints.body: This contract names the online contribution, so a small rate produces a small move.

hints.title: Check repeated updates
hints.body: For fixed online parameters, the remaining target error is multiplied by 1-rate on each update.

explanation: A partial copy reduces abrupt movement of the target used for bootstrapping. It is an exponential moving average when applied repeatedly to successive online parameters.
The rate convention must be explicit: using a retention coefficient as an online rate reverses the behavior. This operation synchronizes parameters and does not compute gradients.
